language.script_notes: English as national; Aboriginal place names common throughout, especially in less urban areas.

road_furniture.bollard_color: White posts with a red reflector on the front that stops partway (doesn't wrap fully around) and a grey reflector on the back — the red-stopping-at-the-middle detail is what distinguishes Australia from New Zealand, whose red reflector wraps all the way around.
road_furniture.guardrail_type: Varies distinctly by state: NSW/ACT guardrails often end with a yellow background and black diagonal dash.
road_furniture.line_paint: Yellow outside/white inside lines common on many roads, alongside yellow outside/yellow inside.
road_furniture.curb_style: White street name signs nationwide; give-way signs use black text.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Utility pole style varies meaningfully by state — see regional profiles (Victoria's circular concrete poles, South Australia's part-steel/part-concrete Stobie poles, Northern Territory's holed metal poles, Western Australia's yellow signposts).

architecture.roof_style: Single-story detached houses with simple pitched roofs dominate suburban Australia nationwide; corrugated metal roofing extremely common.
architecture.roof_material: Corrugated metal (Colorbond-style) roofing is a strong national tell, alongside terracotta tile in older suburbs.
architecture.wall_construction: Brick veneer or weatherboard single-story houses on individual suburban lots are the default nationwide; elevated 'Queenslander' style houses on stilts in the tropical north.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Muted brick and pale weatherboard tones; corrugated metal roofing in silver/grey or earth tones.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Single-story brick veneer or weatherboard suburban houses with corrugated metal roofs; elevated Queenslander houses in the tropical north; utilitarian roadhouse buildings in remote areas.

nature.vegetation: Eucalyptus (gum tree) forest and scrub dominate nationwide — a very strong general Australia tell; vegetation density and colour vary sharply by region, from lush coastal forest to sparse red-dirt Outback scrub. See regional profiles.
nature.terrain: An enormous, mostly flat and arid continent — a densely populated eastern coastal strip, a vast arid interior (the Outback), and a sparsely populated west.
nature.climate_signature: Extremely varied — humid subtropical on the east coast, arid desert in the interior, Mediterranean in the southwest — bright, high-contrast sunlight is common nationwide.

vehicles.plate_color: Varies distinctly by state: NSW plates commonly yellow, Queensland maroon/white, Victoria/Tasmania/Western Australia blue/white, South Australia black/white, Northern Territory sometimes red-tinged text on white — state plate colour is one of the single best in-country location clues.
vehicles.plate_format: Varies by state; commonly a letter/digit mix around 6 characters.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Dual-cab 'utes' (pickup trucks — Ford Ranger, Toyota HiLux, Isuzu D-Max, Mitsubishi Triton) are disproportionately common — a strong national/regional tell versus most of the rest of the world.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Full range including notable Gen 1 coverage (alongside the US and New Zealand) in some areas; otherwise mostly Gen 3/4 in populated areas.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Very dense along the populated east coast; large genuine gaps across the sparsely populated Outback interior.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Left-hand traffic, English signage, similar bollard base style, similar suburban house construction
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Australia's bollard red reflector stops partway around the post; New Zealand's wraps fully around the back — a reliable close-up tiebreaker. Australia is also flatter and drier overall than New Zealand's more mountainous, green terrain.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Left-hand traffic, English signage, similarly dry scrub/savanna vegetation in parts
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Australian eucalyptus forest/scrub looks distinct from South African acacia savanna once compared directly; plate formats and road furniture differ substantially between the two.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Left-hand traffic, English signage and language
confusion_set.tiebreaker: UK terrain, architecture (dense terraced housing, stone construction) and much greener, cooler climate look nothing like Australia's brick-veneer suburbs and eucalyptus scrub once any landscape is visible.
